podcast.body: Featured on "The Red Album" from 2008, this song showcases Weezer's signature style of short, quirky pop songs, characterized by sharp guitars and pointed lyrics, often with a touch of satire. It reinforces their reputation as a prominent Powerpop band in the modern era. "Weezer from the Red Album of 2008 and Pork and Beans."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: The music video for Weezer's 2008 song "Pork and Beans" masterfully incorporated many of the biggest internet memes popular at the time. This included references to the Afro Ninja, Tay Zonday's "Chocolate Rain," the dramatic hamster, Mentos and Coke, the "Leave Britney Alone" kid, and the "history of dance" guy, among many others. "Under 2008 song, Pork and Beans, incorporated all the biggest internet memes to that point."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: This song was an instant favorite at radio stations due to its quirky nature. The distinctive "chipmunk sort of sound" in the song is Rivers Cuomo's voice, sped up an octave after saying "hey." The video for the song featured appearances by prominent internet stars of the day, capturing the zeitgeist of the moment. "It actually sounds like a timble and type of production."
